Answer: B
Reason: The clinical history of multiple fractures combined with progressive dyspnea and bilateral upper-lobe predominant alveolar opacities (ground-glass opacities on the provided CT) is classic for pulmonary fat embolism syndrome. Unlike cardiogenic edema which is typically basal, or aspiration which favors dependent lower lobes, fat emboli often distribute to the upper lobes due to buoyancy and vascular anatomy.
